description:
FILED s536 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-08) while keying the round board's YAML-Tiny row.

REPRODUCER (scratchpad yt.pl; latin1.txt = the bytes `caf\xe9: x\n`):
    open my $fh, "<:utf8", $file or die; my $s = do { local $/; local $SIG{__WARN__} = sub {}; <$fh> };
    print "1 len=", length($s), " is_utf8=", (utf8::is_utf8($s) ? 1 : 0), " valid=", (utf8::valid($s) ? 1 : 0), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: `1 len=6 is_utf8=1 valid=0`.   PCL (MAIN-READY-76): `1 len= is_utf8=0 valid=1` -- the slurp is UNDEF: the whole read is lost.

WHY IT MATTERS: the :utf8 layer (unlike :encoding(UTF-8)) does not validate -- perl reads the octets and marks them utf8; a malformed sequence is a malformed string, and modules detect it with utf8::valid / utf8::decode / Encode (YAML::Tiny `read_string` dies "invalid UTF-8 string").  PCL loses the data.  The representation half (a string can not be "utf8-flagged but malformed" in PCL) is #1389's family (the utf8 flag); the LOSS of the read is not -- at minimum the read must return the text (each bad byte as its own character, as :encoding does with a substitution, or perl's lax octets) and say what it did.

ROWS: cpan-tests/modules/YAML-Tiny-1.74 t/11_read_string.t row 4 "invalid UTF-8" (reached since MAIN-READY-66/-67, when the file stopped dying at its *PLAN*; blessed s536 by edit with this key).
WHERE TO START: the input layer's UTF-8 decoder (`:utf8` read path in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the readline / slurp of a decoding handle) -- find what it does on an invalid sequence (signal caught and the read abandoned?).  Rule 12: a decode failure that silently drops the read is the worst case.


=== DONE (s536d) -- the no-loss half; the row is #1389's ===
(Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08.)  WHAT PCL DID: every reader caught SBCL's stream-decoding-error in its catch-all (`(error () (%p-read-fail stream))`) -- a readline / slurp / `read` / list read answered undef, `eof` answered TRUE, `getc` stopped: the read was lost (rule 12).  Also under `:encoding(UTF-8)` (perl: PERLQQ text).
FIX: `%p-with-input-decoding` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) around every character reader (%p-read-record -- split into %p-read-record-1 --, %p-read-impl, %p-getc-impl, %p-eof-impl): the error is answered for its FIRST byte with SBCL's `use-value` restart (advances one byte; the `input-replacement` restart RESYNCS and dropped the continuation byte of `\xC0\xAF`): `:encoding(...)` -> perl's `\xHH` text, a UTF-8 character cut off by end of file dropped (perl's STOP_AT_PARTIAL; `input-replacement ""` there); lax `:utf8` -> the byte as its own character.  No restart (not an fd-stream): declines, the old handler answers.
MEASURED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s536d/pr/d1-d4.pl): `:encoding(UTF-8)` is now identical to perl on readline, list readline, slurp, `read`, getc/eof, a record `$/` and a binmode'd handle (`a\xE9b`, `\xC3(`, `\xC0\xAF`, a truncated `\xF0\x9F` at EOF); its warning `UTF-8 "\xE9" does not map to Unicode` is warnings-gated (#221, not emitted).  Lax `:utf8`: `"caf\xE9: x\n"` = 8 characters in PCL, 6 in perl (perl's malformed buffer counts by the lead byte), `utf8::valid` 1 (perl 0).
THE ROW: YAML-Tiny t/11_read_string.t row 4 still fails (one-file run: pass=3 fail=1): YAML::Tiny checks `utf8::is_utf8($s) && !utf8::valid($s)`, and a PCL string cannot be malformed -- the representation (#1389).  Re-keyed #4624 -> #1389 in baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv; not-supported "The per-scalar UTF-8 flag" gains the malformed-string note.  A data-encoded representation was considered and NOT built: mapping a bad byte to U+DC00+b (PEP 383) would let utf8::valid answer false, but SBCL's UTF-8 ENCODER rejects a surrogate (octets-encoding-error), so every print of such a string through a `:utf8` / raw handle would need its own mapping back to the byte (perl writes the malformed buffer's octets back) -- a representation decision for Fable, measured here.
GUARD: Pl/t/io-layers-01.t rows 43 (the strict layer's text, perl's own) + 44 (the lax read is never lost) -- both fail on 84a2e6ec.
subject: SILENT WRONG: reading INVALID UTF-8 (Latin-1 bytes) through a `:utf8` layer answers UNDEF -- perl's lax :utf8 layer returns the bytes as a utf8-flagged string that utf8::valid rejects (YAML-Tiny t/11_read_string.t row 4 "invalid UTF-8")
